Professor '''Ralph Kenna''' (27 August 1964 – 26 October 2023) was an Irish mathematician and theoretical physicist who was head of the statistical physics research group at [[Coventry University]]. He was a specialist in [[statistical physics]], [[complex systems]] and [[Irish mythology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.complexity-coventry.org/people/single-view/detail/Ralph_Kenna/|title=AMRC, Coventry University: &nbsp;Single view|first=Ralph|last=Kenna|website=Complexity-coventry.org|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=436791|title=Physics Tree: &nbsp;Single view|first=Ralph|last=Kenna|website=academictree.org|access-date=2023-07-02}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Kenna was born in [[Athlone]], on the border between counties [[Roscommon]] and [[Westmeath]], Ireland, on 27 August 1964.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icmp.lviv.ua/journal/zbirnyk.79/37001/art37001.pdf |title=50th birthday of Ralph Kenna |website=Icmp.lviv.ua |access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref> He attended [[Marist College, Athlone]] (best leaving certificate, class of 1981) and obtained his B.A. (mod) degree in Theoretical Physics from [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 1985. He also obtained his M.Sc. (1988) from [[Trinity College Dublin]]. He completed his PhD ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) at the [[University of Graz]]<ref name="Graz">{{cite web|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/ralph_kenna|title=Physics - Ralph Kenna|website=Physics.aps.org|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref> under Professor Christian Lang in 1993.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=215645|title=Mathematics genealogy- Ralph Kenna|website=/www.mathgenealogy.org|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref>

==Career==
Kenna was an EU Marie Curie Research Fellow at the [[University of Liverpool]] from 1994 to 1997 and at [[Trinity College Dublin]] from 1997 to 1999. He lectured at Trinity from 1998 to 2002, when he moved to [[Coventry University]]. In 2005, he co-founded the Applied Mathematics Research Centre at Coventry and founded the Statistical Physics Group there. 
<!--In 2019 he was conferred ''Doctor honoris causa''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ralph Kenna {{!}} Institute for Condensed Matter Physics |url=http://www.icmp.lviv.ua/en/content/ralph-kenna |access-date=2023-06-23 |website=www.icmp.lviv.ua}}</ref>  by the Academic Council of the Institute for Condensed Matter Physics of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].-->
In 2018 these joined the Fluid and Complex Systems Research Centre, [[Coventry University]], of which 
Kenna was deputy director.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coventry.ac.uk/research/areas-of-research/centre-for-fluid-and-complex-systems|title=Deputy Director - Ralph Kenna|website=Fluid and Complex Systems Research Centre, Coventry University|access-date=2023-06-30}}</ref>

==Research==

Kenna's research interests relate to field theory, [[statistical physics]] (especially [[phase transition]]s and [[critical phenomena]]) and [[complex systems]] (especially applied to  [[Irish mythology]] and other [[Epic poetry|epic]] narratives).

=== Statistical physics ===
In [[statistical physics]], Kenna is noted for his development of scaling relations for logarithmic corrections.<ref name="PRL1">{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna|first1 = R.|author-link1 = Ralph Kenna|  last2 = Johnston|first2 = D.| last3 = Janke| first3 = W.| title = Scaling Relations for Logarithmic Corrections| journal = [[Physical Review Letters]]| volume = 96| article-number = 115701| year = 2006|issue = 11|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.115701|pmid = 16605842|arxiv = cond-mat/0605162|bibcode = 2006PhRvL..96k5701K|s2cid = 5844607}}
</ref><ref name="PRL2">{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna|first1 = R.|author-link1 = Ralph Kenna|  last2 = Johnston|first2 = D.| last3 = Janke| first3 = W.| title = Self-Consistent Scaling Theory for Logarithmic-Correction Exponents| journal = [[Physical Review Letters]]| volume = 97| article-number = 155702| year = 2006|issue = 15|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.155702|pmid = 17155337|arxiv = cond-mat/0608127|bibcode = 2006PhRvL..97o5702K|s2cid = 7648192}}</ref> Already in his PhD Thesis<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna|first1 = R.|author-link1 = Ralph Kenna|  last2 = Lang|first2 = C.B.| title = Finite-Size Scaling and the Zeroes of the Partition Function in the <math>\varphi^4_4</math> Model| journal = [[Physics Letters B]]| volume = 264| page = 396| year = 1991|issue = 3–4|doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(91)90367-Y|bibcode = 1991PhLB..264..396K| url = https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/037026939190367Y |url-access = subscription}}</ref> he introduced a [[renormalization group]] basis for finite-size scaling (FSS) for logarithmic corrections at the upper critical dimension and, with Bertrand Berche, he extended this to higher dimensions in 2012.<ref name="sciencedirect.com">{{Cite journal|last1 = Berche| first1 = B.| last2 = Kenna|first2 = R.|author-link2 = Ralph Kenna|last3 = Walter|first3 = J.-C.| title = Hyperscaling above the upper critical dimension| journal = [[Nuclear Physics B]]| volume = 865| pages = 115–132| year = 2012| issue = 1|doi = 10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2012.07.021|arxiv = 1402.1657|bibcode = 2012NuPhB.865..115B|s2cid = 119216957| url = https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0550321312004063 }}</ref>
They proposed that universality lives at the pseudocritical point instead of at the critical point and a new form for hyperscaling, valid in high dimensions.<ref name="sciencedirect.com"/> This led to the introduction of the new [[critical exponent]] ϙ ([[Koppa (letter)|koppa]]) and its logarithmic counterpart ϙ&#x0302; (ϙ-hat or koppa-hat)<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna| first1 = R.|author-link1 = Ralph Kenna|last2 = Berche|first2 = B.| title = A new critical exponent ϙ and its logarithmic counterpart| journal = [[Condensed Matter Physics]]| volume = 16| article-number = 23601| year = 2013| doi = 10.5488/CMP.16.23601|s2cid = 118152535| url = https://www.icmp.lviv.ua/journal/zbirnyk.74/23601/art23601.pdf }}</ref> to govern the finite-size dependence of the correlation length and a new form for FSS, called QFSS,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna| first1 = R.|author-link1 = Ralph Kenna|last2 = Berche|first2 = B.|title = A new critical exponent ϙ and its logarithmic counterpart|journal = [[Condensed Matter Physics]]|volume = 16|article-number = 23601|year = 2013| doi = 10.5488/CMP.16.23601|s2cid = 118152535|url = https://www.icmp.lviv.ua/journal/zbirnyk.74/23601/art23601.pdf }}</ref> to replace standard prescription above the upper critical dimension.  Fourier analysis showed two regimes that control finite systems in high dimensions instead of Landau scaling.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Flores-Sola| first1 = E.|last2 = Berche|first2 = B.|last3 = Kenna|first3 = R.|author-link3 = Ralph Kenna|last4 = Weigl| first4 = M. |title = Role of Fourier modes in finite-size scaling above the upper critical dimension|journal = [[Physical Review Letters]]|volume = 116|article-number = 115701|year = 2016| issue = 11|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.115701|pmid = 27035310|arxiv = 1511.04321|bibcode = 2016PhRvL.116k5701F|s2cid = 206271579}}</ref> The Q sector is affected by dangerous irrelevant variables and the Gaussian, or G, sector (G) is not but both are physical. The pseudocritical point resides in the Q sector while the critical point itself may be either Q or G.<ref>{{cite book |first1=R. |last1=Kenna |first2=B. |last2=Berche |chapter=Scaling and Finite-Size Scaling above the Upper Critical Dimension |title=Order, Disorder, and Criticality: Advanced Problems of Phase Transition Theory| editor-last=Holovatch | editor-first=Yurij |volume=4 |publisher=World Scientific |location=Singapore |year=2015 |isbn=978-981-4632-67-6 }}</ref>

Formal similarities between spin systems on lattices and on scale-free networks mean an analogy between dimensionality and power-law decay of the node degree distribution there. Logarithmic corrections at critical values<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Palchykov| first1 = C.|last2 = von Ferber|first2 = C.|last3 = Folk|first3 = R.|last4 = Holovatch|first4 = Yu. |last5 = Kenna|first5 = R.|author-link5 = Ralph Kenna|title = Critical phenomena on scale-free networks: logarithmic corrections and scaling functions|journal = [[Physical Review E]]|volume = 82|article-number = 011145|year = 2010| issue = 1 Pt 1|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevE.82.011145|pmid = 20866603|arxiv = 1004.0097|bibcode = 2010PhRvE..82a1145P|s2cid = 14311802|url = https://journals.aps.org/pre/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevE.82.011145 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Krasnytska| first1 = M.|last2 = Berche|first2 = B.|last3 = Holovatch|first3 = Yu. |last4 = Kenna|first4 = R.|author-link4 = Ralph Kenna|title = Partition function zeros for the Ising model on complete graphs and on annealed scale-free networks|journal = [[J. Phys. A]]|volume = 49|article-number = 135001|year = 2016| issue = 13|doi = 10.1088/1751-8113/49/13/135001|arxiv = 1510.00534|bibcode = 2016JPhA...49m5001K|s2cid = 119280739|url = https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1751-8113/49/13/135001 }}</ref> also obey the scaling relations developed by Kenna in 2006.<ref name="PRL1"/><ref name="PRL2"/>

in two dimensions; long-range models in various diensions; spin glasses in six dimensions; percolation in six dimensons; the Yang-Lee edge in siz imensions; lattice animals in 8 dimensions; and the n-colour Ashkin-Teller model in two dimensions are contained in.<ref>R. Kenna, Universal scaling relations for logarithmic-correction exponents, invited contribution to "Order, Disorder, and Criticality:

Kenna's  work on [[percolation theory]] in high dimensions and [[spin model]]s on annealed [[scale-free network]]s has featured in the [[Institute of Physics]] News.<ref>{{cite news |last=Brown |first=Phil |date=21 July 2017 |title=Where physics and mathematics meet for coffee |url=https://jphysplus.iop.org/2017/07/21/percolation-where-physics-and-mathematics-meet-for-coffee/ |work= |location= |access-date=8 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical<!--not stated--> |date=17 February 2016 |title=Interview with Mariana Krasnytska, Bertrand Berche, Ralph Kenna and Yurij Holovatch |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/1751-8121/page/Interview-with-Krasnytska-et-al#skip-to-content-link-target |work= |location= |access-date=8 July 2013}}</ref>

=== Complex systems===
In 2010, with Bertrand Berche, Kenna quantified the notion of [[critical mass]] of academic research groups.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna| first1 = MR|last2 = Berche| first2 = B.|title = The extensive nature of group quality|journal = [[EPL (journal)|EPL]]|volume = 90|article-number = 58002| year = 2010|issue = 5|doi = 10.1209/0295-5075/90/58002|arxiv = 1004.3155|bibcode = 2010EL.....9058002K|s2cid = 53622739|url = https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/90/58002 }}</ref>
Using data from the UK's [[Research Assessment Exercise]] 2008 and the French counterpart ([[AERES]]) they tracked how [[research group]] quality depends on the size of the group.<ref>{{cite news |last=Jump|first=Paul|date=2010-07-08 |title= Truth in numbers: study pinpoints 'critical mass' for research success |url= https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/truth-in-numbers-study-pinpoints-critical-mass-for-research-success/412390.article?storycode=412390|work= |location= |access-date=2023-07-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Hendy|first=Shaun|date=2010-10-20 |title= Critical mass or is mass critical? |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/education/critical-mass-or-is-mass-critical/5UFOWR3RRE5E5H4LMLAALZW4IY/?c_id=466&objectid=10681836|work= |location= |access-date=2023-07-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1= Kennna|first1= Ralph|last2= Berche|first2= Bertrand|date= |title= Masse critique et Groupes de Recherche |url= http://www.sauvonsluniversite.com/spip.php?article4808|work= |location= | access-date=2023-07-06}}</ref> They found quality rises linearly with group size up to a point which they later identified as akin to the [[Dunbar number]] in anthropology. Critical mass, defined as the minimum size a group needs to achieve to be sustainable, is half that size.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna| first1 = R.|last2 = Berche| first2 = B.|title = Critical mass and the dependency of research quality on group size|journal = [[Scientometrics]]|volume = 86|pages = 527–540| year = 2011|issue = 2|doi = 10.1007/s11192-010-0282-9|arxiv = 1006.0928|s2cid = 37876062|url = https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11192-010-0282-9 }}</ref> Subsequently, with Olesya Mryglod and Yurij Holovatch, Kenna and Berche used scientometrics to predict the outcome of the UK's [[Research Excellence Framework]] 2014.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Mryglod| first1 = O.|last2 = Kenna| first2 = R.|last3 = Holovatch| first3 = Y.|last4 = Berche| first4 = B.|title = Predicting Results of the Research Excellence Framework using departmental h-Index|journal = [[Scientometrics]]|volume = 102|pages = 2165–2180| year = 2015|issue = 3|doi = 10.1007/s11192-014-1512-3|arxiv = 1411.1996|s2cid = 255006888|url = https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11192-014-1512-3 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Mryglod| first1 = O.|last2 = Kenna| first2 = R.|last3 = Holovatch| first3 = Y.|last4 = Berche| first4 = B.|title = Predicting Results of the Research Excellence Framework using departmental h-Index - revisited|journal = [[Scientometrics]]|volume = 104|pages = 1013–1017| year = 2015|issue = 3|doi = 10.1007/s11192-015-1567-9|arxiv = 1501.07857|s2cid = 255014082|url = https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11192-015-1567-9 }}</ref> They found that correlations between metrics and peer review are poor and the former  cannot reliably be used to replace the latter.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/the-predicted-results-for-the-2014-ref-are-in/2017192.article#commentsubmitted|title=The predicted results for the 2014 ref aret in|date=27 November 2014|website=www.timeshighereducation.com|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref> This went some way to halting the overuse of metrics at the [[Research Excellence Framework]] 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://results2021.ref.ac.uk/impact/46a76f90-7a5e-4606-94ce-a51d96c1d565?page=1|title=Counting what Counts Confidently (CCC)|date=31 March 2021|website=ref.ac.uk|access-date=2021-03-31}}.</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Jump|first=Paul|date=2014-11-27 |title= The (predicted) results for the 2014 REF are in |url= https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/the-predicted-results-for-the-2014-ref-are-in/2017192.article |work= |location= |access-date=2023-07-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Jump |first=Paul |date=5 September 2015 |title=Can the research excellence framework run on metrics?  |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/can-the-research-excellence-framework-ref-run-on-metrics |work= |location= |access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= Burke|first= Maria|date=2014-12-15 |title= Can research quality be predicted by metrics? |url= https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/can-research-quality-be-predicted-by-metrics/8077.article |work= |location= |access-date=2023-07-06}}</ref>

=== Comparative mythology ===
In [[comparative mythology]] Kenna is noted for pioneering the usage of [[complex network]]s in the study of Irish and other mythologies. His first paper<ref name="universal">{{Cite journal|last1 = Kenna|first1 = R.|author-link1 = Ralph Kenna| last2 = MacCarron|first2 = P.|title = Universal properties of mythological networks|journal = [[EPL (journal)|EPL]]|volume = 99|article-number = 28002| year = 2012|issue = 2|doi = 10.1209/0295-5075/99/28002|arxiv = 1205.4324|bibcode = 2012EL.....9928002M|s2cid = 751459|url = https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/99/28002 }}</ref> on the topic was downloaded over 30,000 times in 10 years, a record<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Mryglod|first1 = O.|last2 = Kenna| first2 = R.|last3 = Holovatch| first3 = Y.|title = Is your EPL attractive? Classification of publications through download statistics|journal = [[Europhysics Letters]]|volume = 108|article-number = 50011| year = 2014|issue = 5|doi = 10.1209/0295-5075/108/50011|arxiv = 1409.7889|bibcode = 2014EL....10850011M|s2cid = 17216146|url = https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/108/50011 }}</ref> for Europe's flagship letters journal in physics, and resulted in considerable media coverage in international press.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eps.org/page/publications|title=Publications - European Physical Society (EPS) }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Colins |first=Nick |date=25 July 2012 |title=Beowulf and Iliad 'more plausible than Shakespeare' |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/9423516/Beowulf-and-Iliad-more-plausible-than-Shakespeare.html |work= |location= |access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author= |date=25 July 2012 |title=Gods and dragon myths 'more realistic than Harry' |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/books/article/gods-and-dragon-myths-more-realistic-than-harry-cqjmmhcqn69 |work= |location= |access-date=7 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= Carbery  |first=Genevieve |date= 26 Jul 2012 |title= Jul 26 2012 |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/study-finds-numbers-add-up-in-irish-epic-1.727798 |work= |location= |access-date=7 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= Czepel |first=Robert |date=27 July 2012 |title=Heldenreise trifft Netzwerktheorie |url=https://sciencev2.orf.at |work= |location= |access-date=7 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= Langenbach |first= Jürgen |date= 31 July 2012 |title=Ist Beowulf klarer als Shakespeare? |url=https://www.diepresse.com/1273804/ist-beowulf-klarer-als-shakespeare |work= |location= |access-date= 7 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--not stated--> |date= 1 August 2012 |title=Sociální Sítě v eposech naznačují: Achilles možná Existoval |url=https://www.national-geographic.cz/clanky/socialni-site-v-eposech-naznacuji-achilles-mozna-existoval.html |work= |location= |access-date= 7 July 2023}}</ref> Other major works include investigations into  the

                         |doi = 10.1142/S0219525916500089|arxiv = 1610.00142|s2cid = 19540179
                         |url = https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/10.1142/S0219525916500089 }}</ref> were the focus of the next subject of study with conclusions broadly in line with the view they were misappropriated from Irish sources.<ref>{{cite news |last= |first= |date=21 October 2016 |title=Ossian poems a hoax |url=https://www.deadlinenews.co.uk/2016/10/21/ossian-poems-hoax/ |work= |location= }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= Siggins |first= Lorna |date= 22 October 2016 |title= Scottish bard Ossian 'fabricated' from Irish mythology |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ireland/irish-news/scottish-bard-ossian-fabricated-from-irish-mythology-1.2838550 |work= |location= |access-date= 7 July 2023}}</ref> The Viking Age in Ireland as portrayed in [[Cogadh Gaedhel re Gallaibh]] was next tackled by Kenna's team.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Yose| first1 = J.|last2 = Kenna| first2 = R.|last3 = MacCarron| first3 = M.|last4 = MacCarron| first4 = P.|title = Network Analysis of the Viking Age in Ireland as portrayed in Cogadh Gaedhel re Gallaibh|journal = [[Royal Society Open Science]]|volume = 5|article-number = 171024| year = 2018|issue = 1|doi = 10.1098/rsos.171024|doi-access = free|pmid = 29410814|pmc = 5792891}}</ref> They developed a measure to place hostility on a spectrum between civil war and international conflict. Their findings<ref>{{cite news |last= Enright  |first=Seamus |date=27 January 2018 |title=Breifne king's role in battle doesn't add up |url= https://www.anglocelt.ie/2018/01/27/breifne-kings-role-in-battle-doesnt-add-up/ |work= |location= }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--not stated--> |date=27 January 2018 |title= The Battle of Clontarf in 1014: an analysis by a theoretical physicist and mathematician |url=https://politics.ie/threads/the-battle-of-clontarf-in-1014-an-analysis-by-a-theoretical-physicist-and-mathematician.261853/ |work= Politics.ie |location= }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= |first= |date= |title=Battle of Clontarf: It's a mathematical question |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/heritage/battle-of-clontarf-it-s-a-mathematical-question-1.3365898 |work= |location= }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--not stated--> |date=24 January 2018 |title=Who was actually fighting whom at Clontarf in 1014? |url=https://www.rte.ie/radio/radio1/clips/21305694/ |work= |location= }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--not stated--> |date=24 January 2018 |title=Network science shines new light on Battle of Clontarf |url=https://www.rte.ie/news/newslens/2018/0124/935551-battle-of-clontarf/ |work= |location= }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= O'Sullivan |first=Kevin |date= 24 January 2018 
 |title= Battle of Clontarf: It's a mathematical question
|url= http://www.jacobin.irish/clontarf.pdf |work= |location= |access-date= 7 July 2023}}</ref> quantified and supported the traditional view of the Viking age in Ireland as one of international conflict and challenged recent revisionist claims. 
A study of  the character [[Fraoch]] identified quantifiable differences between the two parts of his story, supporting the suggestion it was set to writing by two different scribes, one of whom embellished the tale.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Janickyj| first1 = M.|last2 = Curley| first2 = D.|last3 = Maccarron| first3 = P.|last4 = McCarthy| first4 = M.|last5 = Yose| first5 = J.|last6 = Kenna| first6 = R.|title = The enigmatic Fráoch and his eponymous tale — network analysis of an early irish heroic romance|journal = [[Advances in Complex Systems]]|volume = 25|page = 2240006| year = 2022|issue = 5n06|doi = 10.1142/S0219525922400069|s2cid = 250962477|doi-access = free}}</ref> 
Kenna and co-workers also studied Ukrainian mythology.
They compared the Kyiv bylyny cycle to other prominent European epics to identify universal and distinguishing properties of its social networks.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Sarkanych| first1 = P.|last2 = Fedorak| first2 = F.|last3 = Holovatch| first3 = Yu.|last4 = MacCarron| first4 = P.|last5 = Yose| first5 = J.|last6 = Kenna| first6 = R.|title = Network analysis of the Kyiv bylyny cycle -- east Slavic epic narratives|journal = [[Advances in Complex Systems]]|volume = 25|page = 2240007| year = 2023|issue = 5n06|doi = 10.1142/S0219525922400070|doi-access = free|arxiv = 2203.10399}}</ref>
Kenna's team developed  mathematical and statistical methods to probe how a modern complex narrative - namely [[George R. R. Martin]]'s epic novels, [[A Song of Ice and Fire]] - achieved broad acclaim without surrendering to the need for reductionist simplifications.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Gessey-Jones| first1 = T.|last2 = Connaughton| first2 = C.|last3 = Dunbar| first3 = R.|last4 = Kenna| first4 = R.|last5 = MacCarron| first5 = P.|last6 = O'Conchobhair | first6 = C.|last7 =Yose| first7 = J. |title = Narrative structure of A Song of Ice and Fire creates a fictional world with realistic measures of social complexity |journal = [[PNAS]]|volume = 117|pages =28582–28588| year = 2020|issue = 46|doi = 10.1073/pnas.2006465117| pmid = 33139549| pmc = 7682562| doi-access = free| arxiv = 2012.01783| bibcode = 2020PNAS..11728582G}}</ref> This and other works on [[narratology]] led to sustained media interest.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://historynewsnetwork.org/article/148218|title=Padraig Mac Carron and Ralph Kenna: If Achilles Used Facebook...|website=Historynewsnetwork.org|date=8 September 2012 |access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/gb/book/9783319394435|title=Maths Meets Myths: Quantitative Approaches to Ancient Narratives - Ralph Kenna |publisher=Springer.com|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/07/120725090933.htm|archive-url=http://arquivo.pt/wayback/20160314151004/http://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/07/120725090933.htm|archive-date=2016-03-14|title=Physicists study Homer's Iliad and other classics for hidden truths |website=Science Daily}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/books/news/ossian-literary-hoax-james-macpherson-fingal-mathematics-social-network-study-a7371806.html|title=The truth behind the world's greatest literary hoax|date=20 October 2016|website=Independent.co.uk|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref>
<!--
In [[comparative mythology]] Kenna has used quantitative approaches to track the evolution of ancient narratives such as Homer's ''[[Homer's odyssey|Iliad]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://historynewsnetwork.org/article/148218|title=Padraig Mac Carron and Ralph Kenna: If Achilles Used Facebook...|website=Historynewsnetwork.org|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/gb/book/9783319394435|title=Maths Meets Myths: Quantitative Approaches to Ancient Narratives - Ralph Kenna |website=Springer.com|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/07/120725090933.htm|archive-url=http://arquivo.pt/wayback/20160314151004/http://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/07/120725090933.htm|archive-date=2016-03-14|title=Physicists study Homer's Iliad and other classics for hidden truths |website=Science Daily}}
</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/books/news/ossian-literary-hoax-james-macpherson-fingal-mathematics-social-network-study-a7371806.html|title=The truth behind the world's greatest literary hoax|date=20 October 2016|website=Independent.co.uk|access-date=2016-11-15}}</ref>

==Awards, grants and honours==
Kenna was awarded a [[Council of Europe]] scholarship to study in Austria where his PhD was then fully funded by a grant from the [[Austrian Science Fund]] <!--(Fonds zur Förderung der wissenschaftlichen Forschung in Österreich)
--> (1990–1993). He twice held EU Marie Curie Research Fellowships (1994–1997 at the [[University of Liverpool]]  and in 1997 at [[Trinity College Dublin]]). He also held an [[Enterprise Ireland]] Fellowship while in Trinity (1997–1999). In 2004 Kenna became Member of the [[Institute of Physics]] and in 2011 he was elected Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]]. He held a number of grants throughout the years, including from the [[Leverhulme Trust]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/listings?field_grant_scheme_target_id=13 |title=Grant listing |date= 17 September 2010|website=leverhulme.ac.uk|access-date=2023-07-02}}</ref>  (2010–2013) and [[European Science Foundation]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://users.complexity-coventry.org/~kenna/MMM2014.html|title=MMM2014|date=1 February 2012|website=complexity-coventry.org|access-date=2023-07-02}}</ref> (2014), to support his work on [[comparative mythology]]. Kenna held or supported a number of [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions]] including an FP7 International Research Staff Exchange Scheme<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/295302|title=SPIDER|date=1 February 2012|website = cordis.europa.eu|access-date=2023-07-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://ec.europa.eu/research-and-innovation/en/projects/success-stories/all/complexity-science-comes-aid-humanities|title=Success story|date=3 May 2019|website = ec.europa.eu|access-date=2023-07-02}}</ref>  with Christian von 
Ferber (2012–2016; 2014–2018) and an FP7-Marie Curie International Incoming Fellowship<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/300206 |title=RAVEN|date=1 April 2013|website = cordis.europa.eu|access-date=2023-07-02}}</ref> for Dr Nikolay Izmailyan to visit him in Coventry (2013–2015). Kenna has been supported by Armenian State Committee of Science Thematic Grants <!--and Armenian Ministry of Education, Science, Culture--> to collaborate with Nerses Izmailyan (2021–2025). In 2019 Kenna was awarded Doctor honoris causa by the Academic Council of the Institute for Condensed Matter Physics of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]]. His certificate of election reads:<ref name="Doc">{{Cite web |title=Ralph Kenna {{!}} Institute for Condensed Matter Physics |url=http://www.icmp.lviv.ua/en/content/ralph-kenna |access-date=2023-06-23 |website=www.icmp.lviv.ua}}</ref>

{{centred pull quote|By the decision of the Academic Council of the ICMP of the National Acad. Sci. of Ukraine of February 11, 2019 the title of Doctor honoris causa was conferred on Ralph Kenna (Coventry, England) for the studies which provided explanation of scaling and universality in complex systems of many interacting agents, pioneering interdisciplinary applications of statistical physics as well as for his personal initiative in different forms of collaboration with Ukraine and his engagement in preparation of young scientists.<ref name="Doc"/>}}

In 2023 Kenna was selected as Member of the [[London Mathematical Society]] Research Policy Committee.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/about/committees/research-policy-committee | title=Research Policy Committee &#124; London Mathematical Society }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kenna was first child of Pat Kenna<ref name=AboutDad>{{cite web|url=https://rip.ie/death-notice/patrick-pat-kenna-athlone-roscommon/88740/|title=Patrick Kenna: Death Notice|publisher=RIP.IE|date=7 November 2009|access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref> and Irene Kenna (née Benson).<ref name="rip" />
<!--His brother is a businessman and his sister is a bee-keeper. 
-->
Kenna had an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in 2017.<ref name=AboutMe>{{cite web|url=https://theairambulanceservice.org.uk/stories/ralphs-story/|title=Ralph Kenna: Ralph's story|author=Ralph Kenna|work=Web homepage|publisher=Air Ambulance|date=12 August 2017|access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref> 
Despite being 30 minutes gone, he made a full recovery.<ref name=Second>{{cite web|url=https://theairambulanceservice.org.uk/coventry-professor-reflects-on-his-second-chance-at-life-on-anniversary-of-being-treated-by-local-air-ambulance/|title=Ralph Kenna: Second chance of life|author=Ralph Kenna|work=Web homepage|publisher=Air Ambulance|date=12 August 2017|access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref> 
He became fund raiser for the air ambulance who brought him back.<ref name=Rugby>{{cite web|url=https://rugbyobserver.co.uk/news/ralph-to-confront-fear-of-heights-by-taking-100ft-plunge-in-aid-of-medics-who-saved-his-life|title=Ralph Kenna: Fund raising|author=Ralph Kenna|work=Web homepage|publisher=Rugby Observer|date=12 August 2017|access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref> 
He married Claire Dutton in 2015.
Claire has an M.Sc. in [[medical statistics]] and in 2018 published two papers about out-of-hospital cardiac arrests.<ref name=AboutClaire>{{cite journal | last1=Perkins | first1=Gavin D. | last2=Kenna | first2=Claire | last3=Ji | first3=Chen | last4=Deakin | first4=Charles D. | last5=Nolan | first5=Jerry P. | last6=Quinn | first6=Tom | last7=Fothergill | first7=Rachael | last8=Gunson | first8=Imogen | last9=Pocock | first9=Helen | last10=Rees | first10=Nigel | last11=Charlton | first11=Karl | last12=Finn | first12=Judith | last13=Gates | first13=Simon | last14=Lall | first14=Ranjit | title=The effects of adrenaline in out of hospital cardiac arrest with shockable and non-shockable rhythms: Findings from the PACA and PARAMEDIC-2 randomised controlled trials | journal=Resuscitation | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=140 | year=2019 | issn=0300-9572 | doi=10.1016/j.resuscitation.2019.05.007 | pages=55–63 |pmid=31116964 |hdl=20.500.11937/79454 |s2cid=162181633 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>
They had one child.

He died on 26 October 2023.<ref name="rip">{{cite web
| url = https://rip.ie/death-notice/ralph-kenna-westmeath-athlone-534666
| title = Death Notice of Ralph Kenna (Athlone, Westmeath)
| date = 9 November 2023
| website = rip.ie
| publisher = Gradam Communications Limited
| access-date = 15 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url = https://www.westmeathindependent.ie/2023/11/01/great-sadness-at-death-of-leading-academic-from-athlone/
| title = Great sadness at death of leading academic from Athlone
| last = Cusack
| first = Adrian
| date = 1 November 2023
| website = Westmeath Independent
| publisher = Celtic Media Group
| access-date = 15 January 2024}}</ref>
